content: I'll read the test image to analyze the symptoms.

**Observations from the image:**

- **Plant part affected**: Whole tomato plant (pulled up, showing roots, stems, and leaves)
- **Stems**: Extensively bleached/pale cream-whitish coloration throughout the stem length — far lighter than normal green stem tissue
- **Focal lesion**: One main stem shows a distinct, large dark-brown necrotic canker/lesion midway up the stem
- **Leaves**: Severely wilted, browning, and dying; plant has collapsed
- **Roots**: Visible and appearing tan-brown/rotted

**Reasoning through the differential:**

- The **extensive external bleaching of stem tissue throughout its length** (not just at the soil line) combined with a large necrotic canker is the key discriminating feature.
- **Southern Blight** (Sclerotium rolfsii) would primarily show white mycelium and mustard-seed sclerotia at the soil line — the bleaching here extends higher up the stems.
- **Verticillium Wilt** causes internal vascular streaking (cream-brown discoloration beneath the outer stem), not this degree of external surface bleaching.
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum) causes: bleaching/whitening of stem tissue at various heights, cottony white mycelium, and large necrotic cankers on the stems — matching the pale-bleached stems and the prominent mid-stem necrotic canker seen here.
- The complete plant collapse and overall pale stem appearance aligns well with Sclerotinia's ability to girdle the stem at multiple points.
